record.paper_title: Open problems posed at the eighth international conference on fuzzy set theory and applications
record.original_question: Characterize all bounded chains that can serve as the carrier set of an MV-algebra. Is the existence of an involution on the bounded chain sufficient for it to be a carrier of an MV-algebra? Is the property of a bounded chain being a carrier of an MV-algebra expressible as a first-order property?

evidence.quote: Problem 11.1. Characterize all bounded chains which are carriers of MV-algebras.
Is it enough to require the existence of an involution of the given chain?
Is the property of a bounded chain to be a carrier of an MV-algebra a first order property?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An MV-algebra is an algebra (A, ⊕, ¬, 0) of type (2,1,0) satisfying: (i) (A, ⊕, 0) is a commutative monoid; (ii) ¬¬x = x; (iii) x ⊕ ¬0 = ¬0; and (iv) ¬(¬x ⊕ y) ⊕ y = ¬(¬y ⊕ x) ⊕ x. Setting 1 := ¬0 and x ≤ y iff ¬x ⊕ y = 1 gives a bounded distributive lattice order with least element 0 and greatest element 1. An MV-algebra is called an MV-chain if this induced order is total. A bounded chain is a linearly ordered set (C, ≤) with a least element 0 and greatest element 1. Say that a bounded chain (C, ≤) is a carrier of an MV-algebra if there exist operations ⊕ and ¬ on C such that (C, ⊕, ¬, 0) is an MV-algebra whose induced order coincides with ≤. An involution on a bounded chain (C, ≤) is an order-reversing bijection ¬ : C → C with ¬¬x = x (so in particular ¬0 = 1 and ¬1 = 0).

(a) Characterize all bounded chains that are carriers of MV-algebras.

(b) Is the existence of an involution on a bounded chain (C, ≤) sufficient for (C, ≤) to be a carrier of some MV-algebra?

(c) Is the property "(C, ≤) is a carrier of an MV-algebra" expressible by a first-order sentence in the language of bounded chains (i.e., (≤, 0, 1))?
artifact.status_search_result: A general web search did not return a definitive solution to the three-part question of characterizing which bounded chains carry an MV-algebra structure, whether an involution suffices, and whether the property is first-order. Related work on MV-chains, pseudofinite/pseudo-simple MV-chains, and partially cyclically ordered groups provides partial first-order characterizations of certain classes of MV-chains, but no source found explicitly settles the general characterization question.

status_evidence.title: MV-algebras and Partially Cyclically Ordered Groups
status_evidence.snippet: A first-order characterization of groups of unimodular complex numbers and of finite cyclic groups ... leads to a characterization of pseudofinite MV-chains and of pseudo-simple MV-chains.
status_evidence.claim: Partial first-order characterizations exist for special classes of MV-chains, but not a complete answer to which bounded chains are MV-algebra carriers.

status_evidence.title: MV-algebra - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: General reference on MV-algebras and MV-chains.
status_evidence.claim: Standard references do not list a general characterization of bounded chains that are carriers of MV-algebras.
